verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.61
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 8.61

verses.pali: 7. Bhūmicālavagga
verses.english: 7. Earthquakes

verses.pali: Icchāsutta
verses.english: Desire

verses.pali: “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
verses.english: “Mendicants, these eight individuals are found in the world.

verses.pali: Katame aṭṭha?
verses.english: What eight?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavivittassa viharato nirāyattavuttino icchā uppajjati lābhāya.
verses.english: First, when a mendicant stays secluded, living independently, a desire arises for material things.

verses.pali: So uṭṭhahati ghaṭati vāyamati lābhāya.
verses.english: They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them.

verses.pali: Tassa uṭṭhahato ghaṭato vāyamato lābhāya lābho nuppajjati.
verses.english: But material things don’t come to them.

verses.pali: So tena alābhena socati kilamati paridevati, urattāḷiṁ kandati, sammohaṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: And so they sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion because they don’t get those material things.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave:
verses.english: This is called

verses.pali: ‘bhikkhu iccho viharati lābhāya, uṭṭhahati ghaṭati vāyamati lābhāya, na ca lābhī, socī ca paridevī ca, cuto ca saddhammā’.
verses.english: a mendicant who lives desiring material things. They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get them. But when they do not acquire material things, they sorrow and lament. They’ve fallen from the true teaching.

verses.pali: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavivittassa viharato nirāyattavuttino icchā uppajjati lābhāya.

verses.english: And material things do come to them.

verses.pali: So tena lābhena majjati pamajjati pamādamāpajjati.
verses.english: And so they become indulgent and fall into negligence regarding those material things.

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ.
